gaps.sentence: My brother and I ___ turns washing up after dinner.
gaps.explanation: take turns means to do something one after another, alternating.

gaps.sentence: Let me ___ a look at that cut on your arm.
gaps.explanation: take a look (at something) is the fixed collocation for examining something briefly.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ losses of two million last year.
I only ___ sight of the celebrity for a second before the crowd closed in.
gaps.explanation: catch sight of somebody/something means to notice them briefly.

gaps.sentence: The children were told not to ___ so much noise.
gaps.explanation: make a noise / make noise is the fixed collocation.

gaps.sentence: The children ___ us a long story about a dragon.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'a story' and a listener
gaps.explanation: tell somebody a story is the fixed pattern; 'say' and 'speak' do not take this pattern.

gaps.sentence: The storm ___ a lot of damage to the roof.
gaps.explanation: do damage to something is the collocation; past tense 'did' is needed here.

gaps.sentence: I ___ a strange dream last night.
gaps.explanation: have a dream is the English collocation; 'see a dream' is a common learner error.
